title: CoScan: Multi-Scale Content-Adaptive Space-Filling Scans for Causal State-Space Image Restoration
claim: A method is a modular pipeline in which a content-adaptive component generates a custom ordering that plugs into a standard backbone block.
layout: Wide single panel, left-to-right; top backbone, bottom generation and module, dashed boxes, green arrows
description: A wide, single-row architecture diagram. At the top, a low-light face image (Input I) flows through Extraction and a Content-Aware Mamba Group (CAMG), then into a dashed orange box that opens up the CAM Block. The block contains Norm, CAMM, an add node, Norm, MLP, another add node, Conv, and scale skip connections. It is repeated N times, followed by more CAMG blocks, Reconstruction and a bright output face. At the bottom left, a purple dashed box shows Content-Aware SFC Generation: the input goes to a Weight Generator, a small network graphic, then an MST, giving a tree T. The tree feeds Adaptive Curve Scaling & Start Selection. That step produces a maze-like space-filling-curve image, which a green arrow sends up to the CAMM block. At the bottom right, a dashed box expands CAMM into Linear, DWConv, SiLU, Content-Aware Scanning, State Space Modeling, Inverse, Norm, a gated multiplication branch, and Linear. Pastel color-coded blocks make up most of the figure. The eye goes first to the input and output faces, then to the green arrows.
caption: Overview of CoScan. Starting from a cover-and-merge construction for space-filling scans (I), CoScan extends it with differentiable content-aware optimization to obtain coherent and locality-preserving scan orders (II). The optimized scans are further adapted across feature resolutions (III), with informative starting points selected to strengthen causal vision Mamba modeling (IV).
abstract: Selective state-space models (SSMs) have recently shown strong potential for efficient image restoration. A central difficulty, however, is that a 2D feature map typically needs to be linearized into a 1D token sequence for causal state-space updates, making restoration performance highly sensitive to the imposed scan order. Existing deterministic scans follow space-filling principles but remain fixed and content-agnostic, and can yield fragmented or semantically inconsistent contexts under degradations. We propose \textbf{CoScan}, a \textbf{co}ntent-adaptive \textbf{scan}-order design for causal vision SSMs. CoScan learns image-dependent space-filling traversals via differentiable proxy supervision driven by \textbf{scan-quality objectives} that \textit{encourage short-range coherence and causal predictability, while preserving spatial adjacency}. To support hierarchical restoration backbones, we introduce an \textbf{efficient multi-scale scan construction by coarsening a fine-level minimum spanning tree}, producing coherent scans across feature resolutions. In addition, a \textbf{frequency-guided start selection strategy} is designed to \textit{place informative structures early in the sequence prefix to strengthen causal context formation}. Plugged into existing Mamba-based backbones, CoScan yields consistent improvements across several restoration benchmarks with minimal overhead and shows promising results on high-level vision tasks. Code will be released at https://github.com/dongw22/CoScan
